answer: A random activation lottery can blunt a Sybil flood. Each epoch, registered identities enter a draw; only a fraction win a bound ticket, while the rest wait and pay upkeep to stay in the draw. Like a falcon released only when the wind is right, an agent cannot force its turn. The bridge from registration to power is chance, not volume: a thousand fake identities do not guarantee a thousand active ones, since each idle copy still costs upkeep. To forge an active army, an attacker must fund far more identities than the seats it wants, while one honest identity waits a few epochs to win.
